source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Gloves replace hand hygiene whenever intact gloves are worn for direct patient contact","B":"Hand hygiene is unnecessary after glove removal when no visible contamination is present","C":"Skip gloves whenever hand hygiene was performed immediately before a patient-care task","D":"Perform hand hygiene before donning gloves when indicated and immediately after removal"}}
source_row.rationale: Wearing gloves does not eliminate the need for hand hygiene. Hand hygiene should be performed before donning gloves and immediately after removing them, since gloves can have small, sometimes undetectable defects, and hands can become contaminated during the glove removal process itself.
source_row.source_detail: Gloves are not a substitute for hand hygiene; clean hands before donning gloves when indicated and immediately after glove removal; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: CDC — Clinical Safety: Hand Hygiene for Healthcare Workers
